info.name: Limitless Backend APIs
info.description:
Complete, verified API surface for the Limitless cognitive-wellness platform.

There are TWO separate services:
1. Node.js backend ({{baseUrl}}) — accounts, auth, users, assessments (storage), admin, plans, enquiries, PDF storage, payments.
2. AI model service ({{modelUrl}}) — the ONLY source of question generation, scoring/analysis and PDF generation.

Auth flow for a NEW user (mobile app) — REGISTER COMES FIRST, OTP comes after:
1. POST /api/auth/register — name/email/age/gender, and an OPTIONAL `password` field. NO `otp` field needed. The account is created immediately.
   - If you send `password` (min 6 chars), that's the user's real password from the start — `tempPassword` in the response will be null, and no reset is forced.
   - If you omit `password`, the backend generates an 8-character temp password, emails it, and returns it once as `tempPassword` — the app should then prompt a reset via /change-password on first login.
   Either way you get a ready-to-use `token` immediately. The new user starts with email_verified:false.
2. Use `token` as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` right away for the rest of the app — verification is NOT a gate on login/using the app.
3. POST /api/auth/send-otp — emails a 6-digit code (10 min TTL) to that same email. If SMTP is not configured on the server, the response includes `devOtp` for testing.
4. POST /api/auth/verify-otp — flips email_verified to true on the account.
5. POST /api/auth/login is for RETURNING users (email + whichever password is currently active — the one they chose at registration, the emailed temp one, or a later change-password/reset-password value).
6. POST /api/auth/logout (Bearer token) actually revokes that token server-side — call it when the user signs out.
7. Forgot password (existing users): POST /api/auth/forgot-password (email only) then POST /api/auth/reset-password (email + otp + newPassword) — no need to know the old password.

The collection auto-saves `userToken`, `adminToken`, `userId`, `assessmentId` and `userOtp` into collection variables via test scripts on the relevant requests, so you can run requests top-to-bottom inside a folder without manually copy-pasting values.

request.description: Also available at GET / and GET /api/v1/health. Returns { status, service, version, features: { database, ai, stripeWebhook, email }, timestamp }.

exec: console.log('Temp password (also emailed to the user):', json.tempPassword);

request.description:
The FIRST call for a new user — no OTP needed before this. `password` is OPTIONAL:
- INCLUDE it (min 6 chars, as shown) if you want the user to set their own password on the registration screen — it's used as-is, `tempPassword` in the response will be `null`, and `password_reset_required` is false (no forced reset).
- OMIT it entirely to fall back to auto-generated credentials — the backend generates an 8-character temp password, emails it (welcome email), and returns it once as `tempPassword`. `password_reset_required` is then true.

422 if a provided `password` is under 6 characters. 409 if the email is already registered.

Success: 201 { user, tempPassword, token }. `token` is a ready-to-use 7-day JWT — start using it immediately, e.g. Authorization: Bearer {{userToken}}. `user.email_verified` is false at this point; use '2. Send OTP' + '3. Verify OTP' below to verify the email AFTER registering (verification does not block login or app usage).

Call this AFTER '1. Register' to verify the email on an already-created account. Emails a 6-digit code, valid 10 minutes. 60s cooldown between resends. 409 only if this email's account is ALREADY verified (nothing left to do — log in instead).

Response: { sent: true, expiresInMinutes: 10, devOtp? } — devOtp is only present when SMTP is NOT configured on the server AND it is not production (testing convenience). In production with SMTP configured, check the real inbox instead.

400 on wrong/expired code (each wrong attempt is counted). 429 after 5 wrong attempts (must request a fresh OTP via '2. Send OTP'). On success, flips `email_verified` to true on the matching user account (if one exists for this email) — this is what actually marks the account verified. Response: { verified: true, emailVerified: true }.

For returning users. Defaults to `{{userPassword}}` — the same value used in '1. Register'. If that request was run WITHOUT a `password` field instead (auto-generated flow), replace this with the `tempPassword` from that response (or whatever the user later set via change-password/reset-password). 401 on any mismatch.

Success: 200 { token, user, latestAssessment }.

Actually revokes THIS token server-side (not just a client-side 'forget it') — any further request using the same token gets 401 immediately, even though it hasn't naturally expired yet (tokens last 7 days otherwise). Call this on the app's sign-out action, then discard the token locally too.

Success: 200 { success: true, message }.
newPassword must be at least 6 characters. 401 if currentPassword doesn't match. On success clears the temp password and sets password_reset_required to false.

For an EXISTING registered user who forgot their password (different purpose from '2. Send OTP', which verifies email ownership — this is specifically for a password reset code). 404 { error: 'No account found with this email address.' } if no account exists for this email.

Emails a 6-digit reset code (10 min TTL, 60s resend cooldown). Response: { sent: true, expiresInMinutes: 10, devOtp? } — devOtp only present when SMTP isn't configured and not production.

Verifies the code from '7. Forgot Password' and sets a new password directly — no need to know the old one. newPassword must be at least 6 characters.

400 { error: 'Code expired or not requested...' } or { error: 'OTP invalid' } (wrong attempts are counted, same as verify-otp). 429 after 5 wrong attempts. 404 if the account no longer exists. Success: 200 { success: true, user }.
Auth: the user themself (their own userId) or an admin token. Returns the user profile (includes `email_verified: boolean`, flipped by '3. Verify OTP') plus assessments[] (newest first).

Accepts: name, email, age, gender. `payment_status` is ALSO accepted here but returns 403 { error: 'Only administrators can update payment status directly.' } unless the caller's token has role=admin — use the Admin > Update User Plan request instead for that.

Stores an assessment result against a user. Auth: the user themself or an admin — 403 otherwise. 404 if user_id doesn't exist. `report_json` should be the analysis object returned by the model service's /api/v1/analyze endpoint. Returns 201 with the created assessment (id, user_id, report_json, pdf_url, created_at, updated_at).
Auth: the owning user or an admin. Accepts report_json and/or pdf_url.

item.name: AI Model Service (separate service)
item.description: Base URL: {{modelUrl}} — a DIFFERENT service from the Node backend. This is the only source of truth for question generation, scoring and PDF rendering. See {{modelUrl}}/docs (Swagger UI) or {{modelUrl}}/openapi.json for the fully authoritative schema — the bodies below are the confirmed shapes as of this collection's creation.

request.description: age required (10-120). Returns { assessmentId, sections, meta: { source, totalQuestions, scale } }.
responses: 1-500 items of { itemId, value }. Returns the scored analysis object — this is the `analysis` payload later sent to generate-pdf and to POST {{baseUrl}}/api/reports/:userId/pdf.

Returns the raw PDF binary. In the mobile app flow, prefer calling {{baseUrl}}/api/reports/:userId/pdf instead — the Node backend calls this endpoint for you AND stores the result + saves the link on the assessment.
Free/preview teaser report — no payment required (unlike the full report).

body.raw:
{
  "analysis": { "...": "paste the object returned by {{modelUrl}}/api/v1/analyze" },
  "assessmentId": "{{assessmentId}}",
  "brand": { "primaryColor": "#3B82F6", "accentColor": "#6366F1" },
  "teaser": false,
  "sendEmail": false
}

request.description:
ALWAYS pass assessmentId when the user has more than one assessment — PDFs are keyed per-assessment, not per-user, to avoid overwriting/collisions. Auth: the user themself or an admin.

Server-side paywall: if teaser=false and the user's payment_status is not 'paid', returns 403. Set teaser=true for the free preview report (no payment check).

The backend proxies the PDF generation itself — it calls {{modelUrl}}/api/v1/generate-pdf (or generate-teaser-pdf) server-side, so you never call the model service directly for this in the app; you just pass it the `analysis` object.

Returns 201 { pdfUrl, fileName, assessment }. pdfUrl is a public link — download it with the 'Download Stored PDF' request below (no auth needed).
Public — no auth header needed. Replace the filename with the `fileName` returned by the generate/store PDF call. Streams the PDF binary from GridFS; 404 if not found.

Rarely needed directly by the mobile app — prefer 'Generate + Store Report PDF' above. Raw PDF body (application/pdf or application/octet-stream), max 15mb, must start with the %PDF- magic bytes. Auth: the user themself or an admin. Returns 201 { fileName, publicUrl }.

Auth: logged-in user. Creates a Stripe Checkout Session for the $19 Premium Cognitive Wellness Report and returns { url } — open this URL in a browser/webview for the user to pay. Returns 501 if Stripe is not configured on the server.

After payment, Stripe redirects to the success_url and ALSO fires the webhook below server-to-server, which is what actually marks the user as paid — the redirect alone does not grant access.

NOT called by the mobile app — this is Stripe's own server calling ours, with an HMAC signature only Stripe can produce. Included here purely for reference/documentation. Do not call this manually with a fake signature; it will be rejected (400).
Public. Returns active plans sorted by price ascending.
Public contact/feedback form. Fires an admin email notification (best-effort).
Rate-limited to 15 attempts / 5 min. Returns { token, role: 'admin' } — token expires in 12h. Not needed by the mobile app itself, included for completeness / admin-panel reference.
All users, newest first, each with assessments[], temp_password, and mirrored report_json/pdf_url from the latest assessment.
payment_status must be one of: pending, paid, demo, free, trial, suspended. Returns { success: true, user }.
Cascades: deletes the user's assessments AND their stored PDF files in GridFS.
Returns { total_users, paid_users, pending_users, demo_users, free_users, suspended_users, completed_assessments, users_with_report, new_users_24h, mrr, conversion_rate }.
